meta.experiment: Curriculum-accumulation (ASPIRE layer 2 as intended), N=5/arm on two_arm_lift
meta.question: Does a library ACCUMULATED by running the 4 non-lift tasks in sequence improve held-out lift repair (warm) vs an empty library (cold)?
meta.design: Phase 1: run cube_lifting -> cube_stack -> nut_assembly -> two_arm_handover as single-task runs sharing ONE library (skills accumulate). Phase 2: warm (S = accumulated library) vs cold (E = empty) on two_arm_lift, N=5, s_val 100-119 held-out, t=0, pristine baseline. Lift excluded from accumulation (no self-leakage).
meta.run_status: COMPLETE, clean — Phase 1 (4 tasks) + Phase 2 (10 lift runs), no credit/crash failures.

phase1_accumulation.note: The 3 easy tasks pass at baseline (no repair -> no skills). Handover repaired (val 0.95) but admitted nothing this run. Only nut_assembly contributed — a SINGLE, nut-assembly-specific placement-height skill, NOT lift-relevant. This is the design-anticipated thin/degenerate case, and it is the key caveat on the result below.

mechanism_verified_live.warm_injected: All 5 warm (S) reps' skills.md contained the accumulated skill 'seat-at-resting-height-not-target-center'.
mechanism_verified_live.conclusion: Valid test — the accumulated library genuinely reached the warm repair actor.

test.statistic: Mann-Whitney U (S=warm vs E=cold), tie-corrected normal approx

verdict.headline: The curriculum-accumulated library did NOT help lift — the WARM arm scored substantially LOWER than cold on every metric: mean 0.37 vs 0.83, median 0.10 vs 0.85, P(val>=0.80) 0.40 vs 0.80. Cold-beats-warm is borderline significant (z=-1.596, one-sided p~0.055).
verdict.critical_caveat: This is NOT a clean test of a good curriculum library. Faithful accumulation on OUR suite yielded only 1 skill, and it is a nut-assembly placement-height skill with no lift relevance. So the warm arm was seeded with a single irrelevant prior. The negative (and the apparent mild harm) is confounded by the thinness + irrelevance of what accumulated — the suite could not produce a rich, lift-relevant curriculum library to test with.
verdict.honest_conclusion: No evidence ASPIRE's curriculum accumulation helps lift on this suite; if anything a single irrelevant seeded skill coincided with worse warm runs (borderline). Consistent with the hand-seeded skill-transfer null. Layer 2's value remains UNPROVEN — and this suite (3 easy pass-tasks + 2 hard bimanual, whose skills didn't transfer) cannot give it a fair test.
verdict.why_it_matters: The reproduction now has a coherent, honest layer-2 story: cross-task skill accumulation showed no benefit in two independent designs (hand-seeded transfer + faithful curriculum). The demonstrated ASPIRE value on these tasks is per-run trace-guided repair, not skill accumulation.

recommended_next.for_layer2: A fair layer-2 test needs a curriculum that actually accumulates MULTIPLE lift-relevant skills — i.e. more failing-but-solvable tasks that share structure with the target. Our 5-task suite lacks this. Options: add more bimanual failing tasks (M4/LIBERO), or a positive control that seeds a known-relevant multi-skill library.
recommended_next.do_not: Do not brute-force N here — the limiting factor is library richness, not sample size.
